 ICC Women's Emerging Nations T20 Trophy 2026 
 Vishmi Gunaratne’s 49 Guides Sri Lanka Women to Victory Despite Abtaha Maqsood’s 3-Fer
 November 14, 2026 Team Female Cricket 
 Sri Lanka Women produced a composed batting performance to overcome Scotland Women by four wickets, with 11 balls to spare, in the fifth match of Group A at the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Tournament 2026 in Ajman on November 13. Chasing a modest target of 112, Sri Lanka recovered from an early setback and relied on valuable contributions from their top and middle order, alongside a late unbeaten partnership between Kaushini Nuthyangana and Sathya Sandeepani, to secure a crucial victory.
 Vishmi Gunaratne’s 49 Guides Sri Lanka Women to Victory Despite Abtaha Maqsood’s 3-Fer; PC: Getty 
 Darcey Carter’s Fighting Half-Century Rescues Scotland
 After being put into bat, Scotland Women struggled to establish momentum against a disciplined Sri Lankan bowling attack. Darcey Carter was the standout performer with the bat, scoring 62 from 55 deliveries, including three boundaries. However, wickets at regular intervals prevented Scotland from building substantial partnerships. Katherine Fraser departed for a duck off three balls, falling to Nimasha Meepage in the opening over, while Sarah Bryce managed just two off six deliveries before being run out by Vimukthi. Scotland were reduced to 8/2, putting early pressure on their batting lineup.
 Kathryn Bryce joined Carter but could contribute only four runs from eight balls before being caught by Meepage off Sandeepani’s bowling. Pippa Sproul then scored one from 10 deliveries before being stumped by Kaushini Nuthyangana off Sugandika Kumari, leaving Scotland struggling at 26/4. Carter found some support from Priyanaz Chatterji, who scored nine off 12 balls, as the pair attempted to rebuild the innings. Their 23-run partnership took Scotland to 49 before Chatterji was dismissed by Chetana Vimukthi in the 12th over.
 Megan McColl provided some resistance, scoring 16 from 14 deliveries with one boundary. She added 37 runs with Carter for the sixth wicket, helping Scotland recover from their difficult start. However, Sandeepani struck again, dismissing McColl and breaking the partnership at 86. Kirstie Gordon contributed five from five balls before becoming Sugandika Kumari’s second victim, with Scotland losing their seventh wicket at 98. Darcey Carter continued to fight despite wickets falling around her, while Chloe Abel added a quick seven from five deliveries. Hannah Rainey remained unbeaten on one from two balls as Scotland finished their 20 overs at 111/8.
 Also Read:   Nashra Sundhu, Ayesha Zafar Make Big Gains in Latest ICC Women's Rankings Update For Sri Lanka, Sugandika Kumari and Sathya Sandeepani were the leading wicket-takers with two wickets apiece. Kumari returned figures of 2/15 in four overs, while Sandeepani also claimed 2/18. Nimasha Meepage (1/15), Chetana Vimukthi (1/33) and Kavisha Dilhari (1/30) picked up a wicket each, with Meepage and Kumari particularly economical.
 Vishmi Gunaratne Anchors Sri Lanka’s Successful Chase
 In response, Sri Lanka Women experienced an early setback when Hasini Perera was dismissed for a duck off just one delivery, falling lbw to Kathryn Bryce in the opening over. However, Vishmi Gunaratne and Imesha Dulani steadied the innings with a crucial 40-run partnership for the second wicket. Dulani scored 16 from 23 deliveries, including one boundary, before being caught by Sarah Bryce off Abtaha Maqsood in the seventh over.
 Gunaratne continued to anchor the chase, finding an important partner in Harshitha Samarawickrama. The duo added 34 runs for the third wicket, taking Sri Lanka closer to the target. Samarawickrama contributed 24 from 26 deliveries, striking two boundaries, before Chloe Abel dismissed her in the 13th over, with Kirstie Gordon taking the catch.
 Kavisha Dilhari scored two from five deliveries before being caught by Sarah Bryce off Maqsood, while Nilakshika Silva was dismissed for a duck, trapped lbw by the same bowler. Maqsood’s impressive spell brought Scotland back into contention as Sri Lanka slipped to 83/5 in the 15th over. Gunaratne, however, continued to hold one end together and reached 49 from 41 deliveries, including three boundaries and a six. Her dismissal at 109 in the 18th over, caught by Sarah Bryce off Katherine Fraser, briefly delayed Sri Lanka’s progress.
 Also Read:   Sugandika Kumari Completes 150 International Caps with Match-Winning Heroics in Sri Lanka's Thriller With the target almost within reach, Kaushini Nuthyangana stepped up at the right moment. She remained unbeaten on 16 from just 11 deliveries, including a six, and was supported by Sathya Sandeepani, who finished unbeaten on zero from no deliveries. The pair ensured there were no further complications as Sri Lanka reached 115/6 in 18.1 overs, completing the chase with 11 balls remaining.
 Abtaha Maqsood was Scotland’s most successful bowler, claiming three wickets for 18 runs in her four overs. Katherine Fraser and Chloe Abel picked up one wicket each, while Kathryn Bryce also finished with a wicket. Kirstie Gordon and Hannah Rainey went wicketless, conceding 27 and 12 runs respectively, while Rainey bowled one over and Gordon completed her four-over spell.
 Ultimately, Darcey Carter’s fighting 62 and Abtaha Maqsood’s three-wicket haul were not enough to prevent Scotland Women from suffering defeat. Sri Lanka’s disciplined bowling effort, Vishmi Gunaratne’s crucial 49 and Kaushini Nuthyangana’s late contribution proved decisive. The four-wicket victory highlighted Sri Lanka Women’s ability to recover from pressure and successfully chase down a target in the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Tournament 2026.
